a1
In Egypt, Joseph served in Potiphar's house. The Lord was with him, and everything he did prospered.
a2
Potiphar saw this. He made Joseph his attendant, and put him in charge of his whole household.
b1
Potiphar's wife looked at Joseph, and tried to take him to her bed. Joseph refused: how could I do this great evil, and sin against God?
b2
She pressed him day after day, but he refused.
c1
One day, with no servants inside, she caught hold of his cloak. Joseph left it in her hand, and ran outside.
c2
She told her servants, and then her husband, a false story, and showed the cloak as proof.
d1
Potiphar was furious. He had Joseph thrown into the prison where the king's prisoners were held.
d2
But the Lord was with Joseph in prison too, and showed him kindness. The warden trusted him, and put the prisoners in his care.
h1
Joseph did right, and it cost him his position and his freedom.
h2
Yet again and again the chapter says: the Lord was with Joseph.
h3
Doing right may cost you something. It does not take God from you.
h4
Today, do right when no one is watching.
i
Where is doing right costing you something?
